ai.title: Improve hero section responsiveness on smaller screens
ai.summary: Refactored hero layout and typography to fit better on mobile. Replaced fixed height with min-height using dvh in `Section`, removed nested `Section` wrapper in `Hero`, and adjusted heading styles for proper text shaping and wrapping. Updated `IDEDemo` font classes and spacing.

eli5.text: When you open the main page on a phone or other small screen, the large welcome banner and its heading text now fit better instead of being cut off or cramped. The page's full-screen banner no longer uses a fixed height that breaks on mobile; it now sizes itself dynamically so it stays fully visible, and the headline reflows and wraps cleanly with refined letter spacing. You would notice the hero text and the mockup of the IDE below it look more polished and readable on narrow screens, with the IDE demo's toolbar font adjusted to match. These fixes are live today with the web release.

ai.title: JSONObject type uses mapped key syntax
ai.summary: The `JSONObject` type definition in `common/src/types/json.ts` changed from `{ [key: string]: JSONValue }` to `{ [key in string]: JSONValue }`. This aligns the index signature with standard TypeScript mapped types, similar to `Record`. The change affects only the type definition; no runtime behavior or schema validation (`jsonObjectSchema`) is modified.

eli5.text: The way a core data structure is described to programmers has been cleaned up so it matches a widely used pattern, but this does nothing you can see. It only changes how the definition is written for developers; the assistant behaves exactly the same as before, and nothing is added, removed, or made available to any new group today.

ai.title: Rename generic arg in getCustomToolDefinition
ai.summary: Renamed generic type parameter `ToolName` to `TN` in `getCustomToolDefinition` to prevent type rollup errors. Updated internal references and error messages to use `TN` and imported `ToolName` directly. Scope limited to `sdk/src/custom-tool.ts`. Error message now includes specific Codebuff team guidance for name conflicts.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to use a tool whose name happens to match one of Codebuff team's reserved names, the built-in safety check that should stop you and tell you to use a different command instead silently failed. The internal label used to track that check was renamed so the check works again, and the message it shows you now clearly explains that you need a special command instead of a custom tool. This fix is live today for anyone connecting their own tools to the assistant.

ai.title: SDK version 0.3.2 to 0.3.3
ai.summary: Bumped @codebuff/sdk version to 0.3.3 in sdk/package.json. Routine version increment for the official SDK.

eli5.text: The team published a new version of the official developer kit and bumped its version number from 0.3.2 to 0.3.3. This only changes the number printed on the package; it adds no new functions, settings, or visible behavior for anyone using it in a project. Anyone who already relies on this kit can switch to the newer version simply by updating the one line that records its name and version.

ai.title: Fix SDK type tests
ai.summary: Updated `test-types.ts` in `cjs-compatibility` and `esm-compatibility`. Adjusted imports, removed semicolons, and simplified generic usage for `getCustomToolDefinition`. Scope limited to SDK test files.

eli5.text: The assistant's behind-the-scenes type-checking tests were cleaned up so they don't break if a user uses semicolons or slightly different import styles. These are internal test files only developers run, so regular users won't see anything change today.

ai.title: Add MCP support to agent definitions and backend
ai.summary: Added Model Context Protocol (MCP) support to agent definitions and backend. New `MCPConfig` types allow defining stdio or remote (http/sse) servers in `AgentDefinition`. Backend `getMCPToolData` dynamically fetches tool schemas from configured servers and injects them into prompts via `additionalToolDefinitions`. Tools are namespaced as `serverName/toolName`. Scope: `common/src/types/mcp.ts`, `backend/src/mcp/util.ts`, `backend/src/run-agent-step.ts`.

eli5.text: An agent (the automated helper that builds and modifies code inside a project) can now be told to talk to external services called MCP servers. These servers act like extra toolboxes the agent can reach into on demand, so instead of only using the built-in tools, the agent can pull in custom tools defined by whoever set up that server. To use one, a project’s configuration lists the server by name (names cannot contain a slash) and optionally which specific tools to allow, written as serverName/toolName. When the agent runs, it asks the server for that tool’s instructions and then uses them just like any other tool during a turn. This is live today for projects that configure one of these servers; if no server is configured, nothing changes for the agent.

ai.title: Add MCP SDK dependency to common package
ai.summary: Added `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` (^1.18.2) to `common/package.json` dependencies. Prepares core module for Model Context Protocol integration.

eli5.text: The team added support for a standard called the Model Context Protocol into the shared toolkit that powers core features across the product. This lets the assistant connect to external tools and data sources that already speak that same standard, rather than needing custom wiring for each one. It only affects internal building blocks today, so you won't see a new button or behavior yet, but it's the foundation that future integrations will build on.
